lessons.title: Vowel signs 1: া ি ী
lessons.goal: Read consonant + a / i using া, ি, ী, and read the first family words unaided.
grammar: A vowel after a consonant is written as a sign (কার kar), not as the full vowel letter
া (a-kar) goes after the consonant: কা = ka
ি (i-kar) is written BEFORE the consonant but said after it: কি = ki
lessons.tip:
**Vowels after a consonant are written as signs (কার *kar*).** Instead of writing ক + আ, you write ক + া = **কা** (`ka`). Now you can read মামা (`mama`), খালা (`khala`), বাবা (`baba`)!

**The big surprise: ি is written BEFORE the consonant.** In **কি** the hook stands on the left, but you still say k first, then i: `ki`, never *ik*. Find the consonant, then add the sign's vowel: চাচি = চা + চি = `chachi`.

**ি vs ী**: the short-i sign ি stands on the left of the letter, the long-i sign ী on the right (কী). They **sound the same**; the spelling just differs from word to word (চাচি with ি, নদী with ী).

lessons.title: Vowel signs 2: ু ূ ৃ
lessons.goal: Read u / ri signs below the consonant, including shape changes under র, হ, শ, গ.
grammar: ু and ূ hang below the consonant; both say u (spelling only)
ৃ (ri-kar) hangs below and says ri: কৃ = kri
Some letters change shape with these signs: রু, রূ, হু, হৃ, শু, গু
lessons.tip:
These three signs hang **below** the consonant.

**ু** and **ূ** both say `u` (as in *food*): ফুফু (`fufu`), খালু (`khalu`), আপু (`apu`), দুধ (`dudh`, milk), দূরে (`dure`, far). Like ি/ী they **sound the same**; only the spelling differs. The long-u sign ূ has an extra loop.

**Shapes change**: in **রু** and **রূ** the sign sits to the right of র; in **হু** and **হৃ** it becomes a curl or hook under হ; in **শু** and **গু** it folds into the letter. When a shape looks new, find the base letter first, then the sign.

**ৃ** is the sign form of ঋ and says `ri`: কৃষক (`krishok`, farmer), পৃথিবী (`prithibi`, world). Don't mix up কৃ (`kri`, a small hook) with কু (`ku`, a loop).

lessons.title: Vowel signs 3: ে ৈ
lessons.goal: Read e / oi signs, both written before the consonant.
grammar: ে (e-kar) and ৈ (oi-kar) are written BEFORE the consonant, said after
ে has two sounds: e (bed) or æ (cat), learned word by word
Don't confuse ে + consonant + া (= ো, next lesson) with ে alone
lessons.tip:
**ে and ৈ go on the left**, just like ি. Read the consonant first, then the sign's vowel: **কে** is `ke`, not *ek*. দেশ = দ + ে + শ = `desh`; কেমন = `kemon`; মেয়ে = `meye`.

**ে has two pronunciations**: `e` as in *bed* (দেশ) or an open sound like the *a* in *cat* in some words (দেখা in আবার দেখা হবে). Transliteration writes both as `e`, so let the audio guide you.

**ৈ** is ে with a little flick on top and says `oi` (*boy*): তৈরি (`toiri`, ready), পহেলা বৈশাখ (`pohela boishakh`, Bengali New Year).

Warning for next lesson: if you see ে on the left **and** া on the right of the same letter, that's one sign, ো (`o`).

lessons.title: Vowel signs 4: ো ৌ
lessons.goal: Read the two split signs that wrap around the consonant.
grammar: ো = ে on the left + া on the right, read as one vowel o
ৌ = ে on the left + ৗ on the right, read as ou
Find the consonant in the middle, then read the wrapped vowel after it
lessons.tip:
**These signs wrap around the consonant.** ো is ে on the left plus া on the right: কো = `ko`. Find the consonant in the middle, then read *one* vowel `o`: ভালো (`bhalo`), তোমার (`tomar`), বোন (`bon`), ছোট (`chhoto`).

**ৌ** is the same wrap but with a curly tail (ৗ) on the right instead of the stick: `ou` as in *low*. নৌকা (`nouka`, *boat*), মৌমাছি (`moumachhi`, *bee*).

**Don't read it as e + a.** কো never means *kea*. Whenever ে and া hug one letter, it's ো.

Recap of sign positions: right (া ী), left (ি ে ৈ), below (ু ূ ৃ), both sides (ো ৌ).

lessons.title: Vowel signs review: family words
lessons.goal: Read whole family words without transliteration, using all ten kar signs.
grammar: Left-side signs (ি ে ৈ) are said after the consonant
lessons.tip:
You can now read the family words on your own: **মামা, মামি, খালা, খালু, চাচা, চাচি, দাদা, দাদি, নানা, নানি, ফুফু**.

**Reading routine**: (1) find each consonant; (2) look left, right, below and around it for a sign; (3) say consonant + vowel, even when the sign is drawn on the left; (4) a consonant with no sign keeps its `o`, which is often silent at the end of a word.

**Same sound, different spelling**: ি/ী and ু/ূ. **Wrap-around**: ো/ৌ. Next: conjuncts, where two consonants stack with no vowel between them (শিক্ষক, ধন্যবাদ).
